Even though the root cause is likely in the Fortran frontend, diagnostics infrastructure is a plausible companion module because the user-visible failure is an emitted error and the issue summary references required wording/validation of a language rule.

The failing case gets far enough for a normal pass pipeline to exist in one test, while the bad case fails during compilation before optimization passes. If the Fortran frontend lowers CHARACTER allocation/type information into generic tree representations incorrectly, tree/type infrastructure can be the intermediate layer consuming that state; this is less likely than `gcc/fortran` but still plausible for deferred/assumed character length handling.

Pass-trace evidence shows ordinary tree/IPA/RTL passes for the successful case, so the backend pipeline itself is probably not the primary fault. Still, if frontend lowering of allocation semantics into generic IR is mishandled, the shared lowering/GIMPLE interface is the nearest non-frontend module worth carrying forward as a lower-probability candidate.
